paraphrase: Three similes occurred to the bodhisatta: as a wet sappy log in water, or on land, cannot be made to give fire, those who do not live withdrawn in body and mind from sensual pleasures cannot attain awakening, whether they feel painful feelings or not; only those withdrawn, like a dry log away from water, are capable of it.

paraphrase: The bodhisatta then practised forcibly subduing mind with mind, the breathless meditation and severe reduction of food, experiencing extreme painful feelings and emaciation, yet these did not overpower his mind; he concluded that no ascetic has felt more pain, but that by this gruelling practice he did not attain superhuman knowledge and vision, and asked whether there might be another path to awakening.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). Restricted (extreme breath retention and prolonged fasting): summary with the text's own verdict that these practices did not lead to awakening; no method details are recorded.

paraphrase: He recalled sitting in the cool shade of a jambu (rose-apple) tree while his father the Sakyan was working, and entering the first jhāna; recognising 'that is the path to awakening', he saw that he need not fear that pleasure, which has nothing to do with sensual pleasures; he took solid food to regain strength, and the five monks left him in disgust.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). The tree is named 'jambu' in the Pali (Sujato: black plum).

paraphrase: He entered the four jhānas and, with the mind concentrated, attained the three knowledges in the three watches of the night; the pleasant and painful feelings that arose did not invade his mind.

paraphrase: Saccaka says he has debated Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita, Pakudha, Sañjaya and the Nigaṇṭha, and each dodged the issue, changed the subject and showed anger, whereas the Buddha's complexion only brightens under attack.
notes: Reported by an opponent: Saccaka (MN 36). Section refs = SuttaCentral (bilara) segmentation, checked in the local e-text.

paraphrase: Saccaka, asked what 'development of the body' means, names Nanda Vaccha, Kisa Saṅkicca and Makkhali Gosāla: they go naked, lick their hands, refuse food brought or prepared for them or invitations, and eat at fixed intervals of days; pressed by the Buddha, he admits they also at times eat rich foods and so rebuild the body.
notes: Reported by an opponent: Saccaka the Nigaṇṭha's son, answering the Buddha (MN 36, Buddhist Pali canon). Section refs = SuttaCentral (bilara) segmentation, checked in the local e-text.
